title: Count Alternating Subarrays
statement:
You are given a binary array `nums` of length `n` (every element is `0` or `1`). A subarray is **alternating** if no two adjacent elements inside it are equal. A subarray of length 1 is always alternating.

Count the alternating subarrays of `nums`. Subarrays are contiguous, and two subarrays at different positions count separately even if they hold the same values.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers, each `0` or `1`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of alternating subarrays.

examples.explanation: The four single-element subarrays all count. Of the longer ones only `[0, 1]` (the first two elements) is alternating, so the total is 5.
The whole array alternates, so every subarray counts: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.
Only the three subarrays of length 1 qualify.

hints: Checking every subarray is O(n^2) at best. Think about the subarrays that end at a fixed index i.
If nums[i] differs from nums[i-1], every alternating subarray ending at i-1 can be extended by one element, plus the single element itself.
Keep a running length `cur` of the alternating run ending at i (reset it to 1 when nums[i] equals nums[i-1]) and add `cur` to the answer at each step.
